utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Seric, are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes. We are quite ready. The witness is here and we are waiting for him to be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We are applying for a pseudonym and face distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before we have the next witness, I would like to remind both parties about two matters. One is for the -- as for the final trial briefs, I believe that both parties should act in accordance with the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions, which was issued by this Tribunal on the 5th of March, 2002. In this direction, it says clearly the final trial brief will not exceed 200 pages or 60.000 words, whichever is greater. The other matter is that we have received the filings from the Prosecution concerning the rebuttal witnesses. We are expecting the filings from the Defence counsel. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, Judge Clark, Judge Diarra, we are preparing, and your comments are timely of course, and certainly would be in any event but we have prepared, are preparing a motion on the length of the issues for clarification, because of course in this situation we have a multi-accused case and it strikes us as least as a bit of an anomaly that the party with the burden of proof would get half as many pages as the parties -- as the Defence since, presumably, both accused each get 200 pages and that would mean a total of 400 pages of Defence briefs whereas the Prosecution, again with the burden of proof, would only have 200 pages. I'm not asking for the Chamber to issue any sort of ruling at this moment but we are prepare ago filing on that to -- won't come as any surprise I suppose based on what I just said for some upward increase for the Prosecution above 200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I think this Trial Chamber will act in accordance with the filings you will file. Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the witness is moving in, I can say that our response to the Prosecutor's motion for additional evidence, we shall submit until the -- by the 18th of September this year. That is within the next two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. 2 [The witness entered court] 3 JUDGE LIU: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me? 4 THE WITNESS: [Interpretation] I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Seric? Examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. The usher will show you a sheet of paper with your name and your pseudonym on it. If the -- your name is correctly written, say yes, but take care not to mention your name. Just say yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, or perhaps I or other parties will address you by the pseudonym granted you by the Chamber, and that is MU [As interpreted]. Let us endeavour to be as slow as possible and it is particularly important to wait for a few seconds after I finish my question so that the interpreters could keep up with us and interpret all that we say. This is of utmost importance because, believe it or not, we shall move faster in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, one thing to clarify. What is the pseudonym for this witness? It's MU or MV?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] MV, I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as I would like to go now into some particulars of this witness, could we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, were you engaged in jobs that allowed you to receive different kinds of information and reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information about the persecution of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Muslims move from one to the other part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the same happen to Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information whatsoever that Vinko Martinovic and his unit expelled, evicted Muslims from their flats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes. In several instances, there was some information but it had not -- it was not verified, and therefore was not reliable. It all boiled down to hearsay, to grapevine and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about members of some other units misrepresenting themselves as Stela's boys or Stelici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any direct knowledge, any personal experience, with some occurrence of that nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do? Did you check it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes. I remember there was a report that at night, in a part of -- in a building, people were harassed and evicted and that two of Stela's comrades at arms were mentioned. Pursuant to the commander's order, I personally went to the site in the morning and inquired, asked the tenants there about it, and we even organised a confrontation between two comrades at arms, Stela's, that is. However, these tenants stated that those two did not fit, that they looked differently from those individuals who had come the previous night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there were any other cases of impersonation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes. On several occasions, mostly late at night, some uniformed individuals would say they belonged -- may I say that? That they were members of the military police or that they were members of MUP, of the civilian police, of the 4th Battalion, then members of the Convicts Battalion, and some other units which held the positions around town. However, the identity -- however, we were unable to establish whether those individuals really belonged to those units. Moreover, we gained the impression that those individuals did not belong to the units they said that they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Chamber, according to the information that you had, what was Vinko Martinovic's duty, office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Vinko Martinovic, from what I know, held no office, but he enjoyed the authority amongst a group of soldiers from his street and he was -- he enjoyed also the reputation of a brave man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, whilst engaging in the duties that we heard you discharged, did you also do the same thing in 1996 and the beginning of 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will have now some personal questions, so could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- do you have any knowledge whether, during the war, and by this I mean the conflict between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, there were any cases of misuse of documentation by AID, that is whether various documents were forged in order to fabricate facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that done by some Croat secret services too, SIS or HIS, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question because I'm bound by the official secrets act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you aware -- do you have any knowledge whether there was a deal struck between Muslim and some Croatian or Croat secret services relative to the selection of documents used in cases before -- in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Because I'm duty-bound to keep official secrets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I've finished my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, any cross-examination, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So my, my learned colleague was so swift that I failed to prepare my working papers.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Poriouvaev, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Poriouvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, I suggest that we should go into private session for some points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you have to introduce yourself to the witness first.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I will do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Later on, we will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my name is Vasily Poriouvaev, I am a trial attorney and I will ask you some questions relative to your direct examination by Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sometimes, Witness, your information bore title "information A" or "information B". Could you explain briefly to the Trial Chamber what is the difference between information A and B? Is it a matter of credibility or sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly but I think that it was the analysts who divided information that way. People in the analytical sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you cannot explain the difference; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suggest that during your daily activities, you cooperated with military police and crime investigation department in particular; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I did not, at least not personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not just interested in you personally but I'm asking you about your agency, SIS, as an organisation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you don't know? Or you don't want? Or it is also military secret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 629.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't have this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence doesn't have this document either, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's just maybe a matter of confusion. Unfortunately -- this document was admitted into evidence. Can I use it now? Just to show one page? Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may use it and if it's not the document under seal, could we put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, because we can reveal, in such a way, the witness's identity. But I can provide you with my own copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to you take a look at the last -- at the second page, just at the end, just at the bottom of the page. Is your position, title, indicated rightly, correctly, in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. Thank you very much. I did not do it on purpose, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, in response to the Defence counsel's question, you stated that you had some information about the persecution of Muslims in West Mostar, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which units, which army, was involved in such kind of persecutions, expulsion, eviction and so on? Were it HVO units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then who did it? Individuals who were not military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will rise until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, we will start in open session, so be careful with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Your Honour. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 620.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the original document. I suggest that this information was also just drafted by you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, this information, as you see, is dealing with planned expulsion of Muslim citizens. How did you get to know about these facts, which were characterised by you as widespread? Did you talk to Muslim victims? I mean victims of plundering, first of all, of course. Or did your people, your subordinates, do that in the line of their duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I received this information from citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Citizens of Croat nationality or Muslim nationality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- and how didn't you manage to establish people who were doing that, if it is true that they were misrepresenting themselves? Was your staff not qualified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I have already said that, if I remember properly, I went on one occasion to that building where there was -- citizens were disturbed during the previous night and from which we had received information that the names of some, as they called them, Stelici and so, and I've already said it, I even organised eye-to-eye confrontation with two of Stela's comrades at arms to see whether the tenants would recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question was, did you talk to any Muslim victim of plundering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have still two topics to cover and I will not take you long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that Vinko Skrobo unit used prisoners from Heliodrom on the confrontation line, in such a way, imperilling their life and health?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I'm not aware of those cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 718.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to page 2 of the document, just I mean the second paragraph of the document, from above. Did you manage to read this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this document drafted when you kept your position; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I suggest that you knew about the facts that prisoners were used by Vinko Skrobo unit in digging their part of the line, digging trenches or doing something else as indicated here in the information; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, all that I'm asking is that the witness be allowed to read the whole information and that the Prosecutor question be based on full information, because this information says very loud and clear where the work was taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is allowed to read the whole document, especially that particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read it, Witness? So were you aware of that fact --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of such facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, since you have read the whole document, I will ask another question relevant to this document. In this document, it is indicated that the HV company, which was involved in the confrontation line, left Mostar in such a way it created problems for the security of the lines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't know that prisoners were involved in forced labour in other lines, in other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 719.1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "I didn't."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, I would like you to take a look at the last page of the document and the name of person who signed this document. Don't pronounce his name, please, and his position. Is it correct that this man was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was not? Do you mean that this is a false information? A false piece of information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he your superior, immediate superior? You've just indicated in the beginning of the cross-examination who was your immediate superior, and the position you mentioned here in the courtroom is consistent with the position indicated in this document. That's why I'm asking you just to clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: Sir, at that time, I was in the command of the town defence, and this information was done at the SIS centre in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you just mentioned to the Trial Chamber what position you occupied in December, 1993. Maybe we have misunderstood you. I don't ask you to just to give your position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, shall we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe for security reasons, we should do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to now -- to return to the problem of HV involvement in armed conflict in Mostar. So do you continue to insist that HV units were not involved in armed conflict in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't know of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like witness to be shown Exhibit 628.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, was this piece of information drafted by you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read it well. This information is dealing with HV military police being stationed in Mostar, and you also indicate in this information that you have called on your own responsibility the commanders of HV units. You are not talking in this information about individuals. The units and their commanders are mentioned; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't remember this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If your memory fails you, I cannot help you. But maybe I will try to help you somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 292.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, is this your document, witness? I put my question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember, Witness, but in this document, you mention a joint HV/MUP and HVO patrol which was functioning in the territory of Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't mention or you don't remember? You did not mention this fact or you don't remember this fact? Just clarify your position, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't remember this report, and I don't remember ever having such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My final question will be: Is it correct, Witness, that there was some problem between Vinko Skrobo and Mario Milicevic, who were commanders of Vinko Skrobo unit and Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 628.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you lift it down? Now, Witness, do you remember -- did you recall that incident which took place on the 7th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to tender the following documents: Exhibit P292.1; 578.1; 620.4; 624.1; 628.1; 628.2; 719.1; the last document has already been tendered but since there is no decision on the admittance of this document, I tender it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are objections, Your Honour. But considering that there are several documents and we have different grounds for objecting to each one of them, I kindly ask to extend the time allowed for the Defence to lodge their objections in writing. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the document P620.4, and document P624.1, this, during the testimony of that witness, the witness said clearly that those documents were written by himself. So there is no doubt about the reliability and authenticity of those two documents. So we decided that those two documents are admitted into the evidence. As for the other five documents, we are looking forward to your response, and as for the document P719.1, we found that there is no English translation for that document, at least in my binder. We will consider that document when we receive the English translation of that particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually we have a translation, maybe it was some mistake by our assistants not to provide you with the translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. This any way, we will make our decision when we receive the objections from the Defence side Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. concerning with those five documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we will have the next witness, and we understand that the next witness will be an expert witness. We need -- we need to have the statement of that witness at our hands. So could I suggest we break for five minutes? Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that statement was filed with the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution office a long time ago. I believe the Trial Chamber should have it. But if necessary, we are prepared to have it photocopied during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, we have it in our office but we don't think that we could conduct the testimony of the first witness so smoothly so we did not bring it here. So my suggestion is that we have five minutes' break and we'll resume after that. --- Break taken at 4.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I can hear you. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Par. Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, doctor. Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I begin, I would kindly ask you to try to speak more or less slowly for the interpreters to be able to follow and to make pauses between questions and answers. When I finish my question, it would be a good idea for you to wait for two or three seconds before you start answering and speak up, please. That said, would you tell us your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: My name is Drazen Begic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us briefly about yourself and your qualifications?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I live in Zagreb. I'm a psychiatrist. I was born in Vukovar in 1958. I'm a doctor, have been a doctor for 20 years now. I became a psychiatrist 12 years ago, and I have been a registered forensic expert for the past five years. I work at the medical school of the university in Zagreb, as assistant professor in psychiatry. I got my BS -- I got my degree in 1953 -- 1993, and I am a member of the Croatian Academy of Arts and Sciences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, this Defence team contacted you in March 2002 with a request for your expertise. Can you describe to the Trial Chamber what kind of request it was and what was your task as an expert?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: In March of this year, I received a request for forensic expertise from the legal office of Seric and Par and I was asked to review the medical documentation for Mr. Halil Ajanic. I was asked to pay particular attention to certain points, such as whether Mr. Ajanic suffered from one or more psychiatric disorders, how they manifested themselves, whether they were progressive or not, whether a person with such a diagnosis or diagnoses could perceive and reproduce material shown to them, to what extent they were susceptible to suggestion and to what extent evidence or facts described by them were authentic and credible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about an addendum to that request that you received? Was there any medical documentation?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: There was one annex, so-called excerpt from the medical documentation of the regional medical centre in Mostar, describing the course of Mr. Ajanic's hospitalisation in April, 1996, in the psychiatric department, in the psychiatric ward, indicating the psychiatric difficulties experienced by the patient at admission and his various diagnoses, as made in the course of his treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, on the basis of that, you made your report and gave your opinion dated 6th of April, 2002. Is that your report?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. It reflects my expert's opinion based on my review of this medical document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the 6th of March, right? Because the transcript says April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. It was March.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The transcript has now been corrected. Let us now proceed with your opinion and expert conclusion. The first question posed by this Defence was what kind of disorder or disorders Mr. Ajanic suffered from, according to the documentation you received?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: According to the medical documentation, Mr. Ajanic suffers from a variety of psychiatric disorders. First of all, psychosis, probably alcohol-induced, the amnesic syndrome and debility. Those are three completely different diagnoses which, however, can quite plausibly co-exist within one and the same clinical picture of one patient. This situation is not uncommon in our profession. It's called co-morbidity, meaning that one patient suffers from several different psychiatric entities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go through these three diagnoses. Could you tell us what alcohol-induced psychosis is, in fact, and how it manifests itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Alcohol-induced psychosis is a complication of alcoholism. A person who consumes alcohol in excess, over a number of years, becomes dependent, addicted, to alcohol. An alcoholic can develop psychosis in a variety of ways. One of the ways is for him to stop consuming alcohol abruptly. In the event of such abrupt abstinence, the patient develops acute psychosis of a degenerative type. Another form of psychosis results from continued consumption of alcohol unrelieved by abstinence and it eventually leads to a chronic form of alcohol-induced psychosis. Both of these forms are characterised by a range of symptoms, typical of psychosis. Psychosis is a condition in which a person does not absorb reality appropriately. There are delusions in the patient, sometimes of paranoid, persecution-related type in males, they take the form of pathological jealousy. Another symptom is difficulty in intellectual functioning and inadequate social functioning. That would be the briefest description of alcohol-induced psychosis, be it acute or chronic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now what amnesic syndrome signifies and how it is manifested?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: The amnesic syndrome is a condition which can be encountered in various psychiatric but also neurological entities, the clinical picture of the amnesic syndrome is amnesia. Failure to recall certain periods of time. These periods of time can be briefer or longer, with varying intervals of adequate functioning in between them. The onset of amnesia can be abrupt or gradual, both in its beginning and its end. It's important to say about the amnesic syndrome that it has a variety of etiologies, meaning that there is a variety of causes. Any serious disease of the brain tissue and the central nervous system from tumors, bleeding, trauma, and a number of others, could lead to the amnesic syndrome. It can accompany degenerative diseases of the central nervous system, dementia, Alzheimer's Disease or non-Alzheimer's related diseases. It can also result from arterial sclerosis in the brain and also through exposition -- through exposure to those addictive drugs. In our end of the world, it is common in alcoholics, many alcoholics develop the amnesic syndrome over time. This amnesic syndrome can vary in intensity and character and the -- and the intense form of this syndrome is called the Korsakov Syndrome. It is characterised by memory blackouts, which are filled by the patient by confabulation, as we call it, completely made up, invented contents. And this is particularly typical of the form of the syndrome which is induced by alcohol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, could you tell us what mental retardation or debility is and how that is manifested?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Debility or debilitas is a form of mental retardation or -- In literature we often encounter two pieces of information. It's a person with the IQ of between 50 and 59 and 50 and 70. It's a person who can usually complete elementary education, find employment of -- in manual jobs, simple jobs. It can enter into marriage and function but at more demanding levels of functioning, the person starts failing in the emotional, cognitive, intellectual and various other senses. These people are unable of performing more complicated tasks. They demand attention from their environment. Their abstract intelligence is very poorly developed. And the last but not least important characteristic is that these persons are extremely susceptible to suggestion. This susceptibility to suggestion is reflected in the following way: These persons accept suggestions and advice from their environment, even if it jeopardises their material, moral, physical integrity. They are capable of acting to their own detriment, following suggestions by other persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now tell us, in relation to the problems that we just talked about, are they progressive disorders? Do they deteriorate or do they -- can there be -- can they be cured over time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: With regard to the first diagnosis that was mentioned here, that is the alcoholic psychosis, it is a progressive disease. In time, the clinical picture deteriorates at all levels. And a similar thing would hold true of the amnesic -- amnesia syndrome although the latter and the progression depend on the cause, that is on the etiology. When we come to the third diagnosis, that is the debility, the degradation may exist but need not. What is important, however, is that a mentally retarded person cannot recover. That is somebody with an IQ between 50 and 69 or 50 and 70 in time, regardless of social care, cannot improve. That is that individual will remain at the same level or the disease will progress and there will be further cognitive collapse, deterioration over time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, could --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You used the documentation referring to 1996?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, you are being reminded by the interpreters to speak directly into the microphone. They have difficulties to hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And my apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, my question was: Since the documentation that you analysed dates back to 1996, and we are in point of fact interested in the state of health of Mr. Ajanic in 1992 -- in 2002, when he testified before this Court, can you tell us whether the state of his health in 2002 could be better, worse or the same as in 1996?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: If I may say, 1992, I guess it's an error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, the documentation -- medical documentation dates back to 1996.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is to be expected that over this period of time, of six years, the first two diagnoses would be progressing, that is they would be a deterioration, that is a decline in mental functions. As for the third diagnosis, the debilitas it is quite possible that there has also been deterioration in this case, but not necessarily so. I repeat in the case of the third diagnosis, there can be no improvement. The situation may be at a standstill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we then conclude that his health can be either the same or worse than in 1996?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: To put it in simple terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Give us, please, if you can go in depth, tell us something more about these diseases. What I'm interested in is the capacity of accurate perception in individuals suffering from these diseases and their gullibility, that is their susceptibility to suggestion, in view of all the diagnoses that we have heard so far.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: The perceptiveness is indubitably disrupted in cases of alcoholic psychosis and the amnesic syndrome, not only the perceptiveness, the capacity of perception, but also the ability to reproduce the memorised material. In the case of debility, the perceptiveness can also be disrupted to a lesser degree. But the ability to reproduce the memorised contents is significantly disrupted in the cases of debilitas. As for the gullibility, the susceptibility to suggestion, psychiatric patients are different from other patients, that is healthy individuals, because the majority of them are highly susceptible to suggestion. So that the alcoholic psychosis and the amnesic syndrome do not differ from other psychiatric disorders in that respect. However, the mental retardation is the psychiatric diagnosis which shows the gullibility most marked. In other words, we are unable to diagnose debilitas, if we -- if the clinical picture does not include also a very highly marked gullibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from the medical and scientific point of view, what can we say? How reliable can be the information or statement received from such individuals, especially if they are interpreting certain events which happened eight years earlier? How reliable are they?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: A period of eight years is a relatively long period of time. And during that period of time, undoubtedly there can be a change in the state of mental health which then results in an altered reproduction. That is an individual with this diagnosis will give unreliable answers. That is to several -- to this person will answer the questions inaccurately rather than accurately, more often than not. The reliability of somebody's statement is again questionable because every one of these diagnoses will severally affect the memory and learning, and when these diagnoses are combined, then of course, their effect is even more pronounced so that reliability is low, authenticity highly questionable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours. I have finished. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Stringer? Cross-examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm prepared for my cross-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could have just a moment to get organised?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Begic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Douglas Stringer. I'm going to ask you questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Before we start, I'll ask the usher to show you two documents marked as Exhibits 877.22 and 877.23. Dr. Begic, I believe, you'll recognise both of these. One of them is the opinion letter that you wrote in response to the inquiry by Mr. Seric and Mr. Par, and the other document is the medical documentation that you have referred to in your direct testimony. Do you have those? Okay. Now, before we go through each of those documents, Dr. Begic, just some general questions first. We are talking about a gentleman who, as you know, was a witness in this case. Did you have an opportunity to examine that person? Have you ever met him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask to have an opportunity to examine him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the opinion that you've given and the information contained in it is essentially based on the issue that was presented to you by misters Seric and Par? That was the parameters of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct. I analysed a document attached to the request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the gentleman's testimony in these proceedings, was that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. testimony or a transcript of that testimony, made available to you, to assist you in conducting your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown what's been marked Exhibit 848.1. Dr. Begic, I don't expect that you will recognise this but I'll ask you any way. This is a witness statement that was provided to our investigators by the gentleman, the witness. Have you ever seen that document?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not have an opportunity to consider this document in conducting your analysis of his mental condition or ability to give accurate or reliable testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I didn't, no, because I analysed only the medical documentation, which is possibility in the Croatian legal system, and that is not unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So before we talk about the specifics of your analysis, Dr. Begic, I'd just like to ask you this more general question. The testimony and the opinions that you've given, it seems to me, sir, that you've -- you are only in a position to give the Trial Chamber information about the characteristics and the attributes that are associated with the various medical conditions that have been identified. Is that a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the document attached, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the document attached is the one that's marked as Exhibit 877.22. Can I ask you to take that document in hand? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a letter written to Mr. Seric and Par, my colleagues on the Defence bench, over the name and signature of a Dr. Ramo Omanovic dated 26 February, 2002. Dr. Begic, is this the basis of the information or does this contain the information that you relied on in conducting your analysis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is nothing else beyond the four corners of this document that you considered in reaching the conclusions that you've reached?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last sentence of the document indicates that basically the information contained in this letter is the only documentation that they have in respect of this person. So this is really all that you had to work with at the time you were asked to perform your analysis for Mr. Seric and Par; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, would you agree with me that this information, the information contained in this letter, first of all, it is not the actual source medical documentation that one would normally want to have at hand in conducting an analysis of the kind that you performed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is, but if I may add, at the end of my report, I suggested a number of procedures which could be requested additionally. I presume Dr. Omanovic really had no other documentation. He prepared this on the basis of Mr. Ajanic's treatment in the ward. But this document already shows that Mr. Ajanic had been treated at least twice, once in Sokolac and once in Mostar. So I had no reason to doubt the authenticity of this document and therefore I assumed that even after 1996, Mr. Ajanic underwent psychiatric treatment, be it as an out patient or in hospital, and in my conclusion, I suggested that this documentation be presented to this Court or perhaps some other expert witness, among other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I waited for the witness to finish his answer but I'd like to establish whether the Prosecutor is bringing into dispute the authenticity of this document, the source of this document, or is he speaking in general about insufficient documentation? We are simply not clear about this as the Defence team and perhaps even the witness doesn't fully understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in my view, the Prosecution is asking about the contents of this document, not the authenticity of this document. You will have more reached documents [sic] than this I'm not sure, maybe the Prosecution could clarify this issue for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, if I -- I didn't mean to suggest that we challenged the authenticity of the document marked Exhibit 877.22. I don't challenge the authenticity of the document. I do -- I'm trying to ask some questions about simply the extent to which the document refers to other information or other documents which have not been made available or which appear for whatever reason not to be available. And I just wanted to ask a couple more questions about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic -- and tell me if you don't know -- do you know who this Dr. Omanovic is who wrote this letter? Do you know him or do you know of him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I don't know him. I've seen several other documents with his facsimile so no, I do not know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did not give you the actual medical records that were made at the time of treatment in 1996, correct? That was not made available?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I did not get that. I did not ask for it. Because I repeat, in the Croatian legal system, you cannot get some documentation from your colleague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, it seems to me that you're not having had an opportunity to examine or to speak with the witness, coupled with the fact that nothing more detailed in the way of documentation was provided beyond what's contained in this letter, that really, you had only a very, very limited basis on which to give an opinion. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I agree with that, but I have to say nonetheless that at the end of my report, there are some recommendations what else can be done, apart from the documentation. Now, if I may be allowed to do that. So other medical documentation, of course, psychiatric or psychological, be an analysis or observation, and what I would add, which I did not include in my report, would be a hetero case history, it means collecting all the information from next of kin, Mr. Ajanic's next of kin or people who are close to him, who can confirm how does he function on a daily level. So I'd like to add it for the record, because I did not include it in the conclusion to my report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that there are a number of things that could have been done, there is -- there are other perhaps other information that could have been acquired by you that would have enabled you to give a more credible opinion as to the mental condition of this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: No doubt there are ways and means of obtaining documentation, of obtaining records, which would perhaps enable one to arrive at a more accurate assessment and forecast, but I have no reason to doubt either the authenticity of this finding, because from the medical point of view, it is written very logically, and it seems to me that, my at least, clinical experience and also literature, seem to indicate that these diagnoses can be only interpreted in the way that I did in my opinion. Needless to say, all that I've suggested to do would lead -- would result in a better, in a higher grade expert opinion. But again, I say that would not look much different in the general conclusion and recommendation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Dr. Begic, that in fact based on the very limited amount of data you had at hand, that would itself undermine confidence in your opinion and your assessment of the witness? You simply didn't have enough data on which to give a sufficiently well-grounded opinion about this witness?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Apart from this information that one finds in this document, I did not have any other information. I repeat that. But the diagnosis which we see here are very serious, long-lasting and I have no reason to doubt that Mr. Ajanic's clinical picture was exactly as it is shown here at that time in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that another person in your field, equally qualified as you, might in fact conclude that there is insufficient information on which to give an opinion of the witness's credibility or ability to give testimony in 2002? Others might not be able to give an opinion based on the information presented?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the manner in which the Prosecutor asked the question, because he seems to suggest that the witness established the diagnosis on the mental condition of Mr. Ajanic. The witness repeated it clearly several times that he analysed the documentation, he did not examine the man or establish his diagnosis. I object to any kind of questions which seem to involve the witness into a zone in which he seems to have established a diagnosis. The witness did not establish the diagnosis, he did not examine the witness, he examined what the paper said -- says. And I think that the Prosecutor is applying an incorrect approach, pretending that the witness has examined the man, the individual in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I can put my question a different way, Mr. President, if it will assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may rephrase your question so that we could understand you better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another person in your field might well not be willing to give an opinion because the data provided is too limited, because they didn't have an opportunity to examine the witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is not correct. An expert witness should be able to produce his opinion on the basis of just one finding, whether it would be different from mine, I doubt it, but in our legal system, we analyse a document, for instance a testament, which is not a matter, which is all that rare, if you get my meaning. That is another expert witness could on the basis of one document give his opinion too. It is another matter whether that opinion would be different from mine and how much would it be different. Personally, I don't think it would be any different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking -- I want to direct your attention, Dr. Begic, to some of the information that is contained on this letter. First of all, this indicates he was treated in Mostar for an eight-day period, I believe as an in-patient during April of 1996; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That fact alone doesn't give us much information about the mental condition of the witness in, say, 1993, which is when the events occurred in which he -- that he testified about? That doesn't tell us much about his condition in 1993, does it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: You are partially correct because this document says that Mr. Ajanic was treated in Sokolac for about three years, in an earlier period, we don't know which exactly but three years of treatment is an extremely long time and it couldn't have been done if it wasn't really necessary. It also says that he was treated in Mostar. Unfortunately again we don't know when, whether it was in 1993, after 1993 or before 1993. But here we have some data partially hetero anamnestic [As interpreted], which the doctor collected from Mr. Ajanic himself and which testify to a prior psychiatric treatment of Mr. Ajanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This information does not enable you to consider or to comment on his mental condition in the summer of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: You are right. But it absolutely does enable me to discuss Mr. Ajanic as a psychiatric patient who was a psychiatric patient even before 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how do you know he was a psychiatric patient before 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters's correction, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you another question. I think we had an interpretation problem there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not able to comment on the witness's ability to correctly -- to form memories or to recall memories then, in the summer of 1993. All you know is that you think he had been a person receiving some form of mental treatment at some time before then or sometime after then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That much is true, but I cannot not take into account the information about his prior treatment. That's one. And second, if Mr. Ajanic was hospitalised in a serious way for the first time in 1996 and received serious treatment, psychiatric treatment, it is only to be expected that such diagnoses would reflect, negatively of course, his ability to recollect events from 1993 and the period before that. I believe that these two points should be emphasised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, what you've just said, sir, though is an assumption on your part. You really don't have any basis to assert that this individual did not have the ability to recall in 1993; correct? You simply don't know whether this gentleman was affected or not affected in 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct. But I don't know that he was healthy either, according to what I see, it seems that he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, in the former Yugoslavia, was it ever possible that someone could -- someone convicted of crime might be placed in a mental facility and by going to a mental facility, they would receive a much shorter sentence of imprisonment than if they were to go to a prison?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: If I may repeat your question to see if I understood it correctly, you're asking whether I'm aware of anyone in the territory of former Yugoslavia, in order to avoid or shorten his prison sentence, to -- opting for a mental institution instead? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question. It's asking for speculation by the witness about something that cannot possibly have any ground in -- basis in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, don't answer that question by yourself. This witness is an expert witness and he -- I think he's an expert in this field for quite a long time. He must be familiar with the situation in the former Yugoslavia. You may proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, what if I suggested to you that this individual spent three years at Sokolac as an alternative, if you will, to spending a much longer period of time in a normal prison? Is that not possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: First of all, I cannot talk about the former Yugoslavia because I became a psychiatrist in 1990, anything that I would say about this would indeed be speculation but I do allow for the possibility that under the former system, there had been abuses in our profession, in the way you suggest. However, I am not aware of any specific instances in order to discuss it for our purpose here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from as you've done in your direct examination, talking about general attributes of these three disorders: Psychosis, amnesia, and debilitas or mental retardation, apart from the general characteristics or attributes of those disorders, sir, you're not in a position to shed any light on this gentleman's mental condition or mental health when he testified here in these proceedings last January; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not really in a position to tell us whether he had the capacity at that time to recall facts, to recall memories, and to testify about those memories?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I was not able to do that, but I repeat, my opinion is based on the document under discussion here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, are you familiar with a document or a book that's called "The Diagnostic Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders DSM-IV"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to talk a little bit about the diagnosis that Dr. Omanovic made, which I take it you assumed and accepted as being a correct diagnosis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would assist me when we talk about these three disorders whether it's possible to try and place them somewhere within the categories or the codes of the DSM-IV. On the psychosis, it sounds to me as though the diagnosis here is an alcohol-induced psychosis. Is that correct or am I incorrect on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Most probably, the diagnosis is alcohol-induced psychosis, as we see in this first part, psychosis verisimilite alcoholic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that -- is that a disorder, sir, in which episodes of psychosis, then, can appear or would appear in association either with alcohol use or alcohol withdrawal?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: As I already said, in response to a question from the Defence, one of the forms is encountered in the withdrawal syndrome, that is an acute form. A more chronic form appears during consumption of alcohol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, getting back again to 877.22, the Omanovic letter, part of it says this:" The patient was admitted as psychotic case, most probably in the state of alcohol abstinence." Now that would suggest to me, sir, that this is a psychotic episode resulting from abstinence or withdrawal from alcohol.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That was most probably the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, also the next reference here in the initial diagnosis is to the amnesic syndrome or to amnesia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question here, sir, is whether, in this situation, the amnesic disorder is linked to the alcohol withdrawal that has given rise to the psychotic episode.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That is possible, but it doesn't rule out the possibility of other causes either, and these other causes I enumerated earlier. In any case, this documentation is too scant to go into any detailed discussion of other possible causes. Basically I'm saying that we cannot rule out causes other than alcohol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But based on the information provided, really, it would simply be speculation for us to consider other bases or causes of amnesic syndrome?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It would be speculation, but it would still be based on the clinical picture provided by Dr. Omanovic, who observed and treated this person for all of eight days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it appears, sir, then that we have an initial diagnosis linking both a psychotic episode and also the amnesic syndrome to alcohol, either use of alcohol but more likely withdrawal from alcohol?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have a final diagnosis which now has introduced a third term, final diagnosis indicated is psychosis episodica and then in brackets, debilitas mentis. Now, my first question, Dr. Begic, is whether the psychosis episodica that's referred to is something that's different from the psychosis that is included in the initial diagnosis. Different terminology is used. I don't know whether that's a different diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is possible that this episode of psychosis, as the final diagnosis describes it, is just a different picture of the same syndrome that was observed at the beginning of the treatment. It is, however, also possible that this diagnosis of retardation was correct even at an early age, that is from birth, but was diagnosed only after his admission to the hospital due to evident delirium. Both possibilities hold equally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This final diagnosis, and I'm focussing on the psychosis episodica now, as a lay person that tells me or that suggests to me that this is a person who suffers episodes of psychosis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the situation with -- which is possible with mental retardation. Of course not only with mental retardation. There is also a possibility of normal functioning over varying periods of time, but it is interspersed with deteriorations which are psychotic in nature. It can run parallel to schizophrenia and it is a picture presenting improvements and deteriorations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've answered my next question but I'll ask it any way. When one talks about episodes of psychosis or psychotic episodes, that would seem -- that would imply to me also the existence of episodes of lucidity, episodes of saneness, episodes in which the person can function at a more normal level, make accurate memories and to recall memories accurately.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: The person does function at a more normal level, in view of the absence of psychotic symptoms. However, it is not complete normalcy when we have retardation. In a stationary situation, where we have a patient with this diagnosis, when the psychotic episode sets in and is over, he resumes functioning more or less normally but at a less adequate level cognitively speaking than a real, normal person would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, now moving down this letter from Dr. Omanovic, he indicates therapy prescribed, do you see that, therapy prescribed.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Begic, I don't want to you speculate or to tell us what one would expect the therapy to be for someone who has these disorders. I want to know -- I want to ask you simply, do you know what was prescribed in the case of Mr. Ajanic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of the therapy prescribed but what I would prescribe in this situation would be at least three different drugs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the extent to which the therapy prescribed was successful in treating any of these disorders? And again I'm talking concretely about the witness. Not in abstract terms.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then that means, sir, that you do not know the extent to which the witness may still have been affected or suffering from any of these disorders at the time he testified here in earlier this year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is partially correct. What I mean is the following. If we agree about this diagnosis of retardation, it is certain that the man suffered at the time when he testified from all the consequences of mental retardation. It is possible that his problem with alcohol was under control at the time. He may have avoided subsequent delerical episodes but based on this report, all I can say is that at the time when he testified, he must have been in the state of mental health that I described and which is defined by debilitas or mental retardation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to sum up that last point, the psychosis, the amnesic syndrome are treatable, they can come and go, they can get better, they can get worse over time. However, it's the mental retardation that is going to be the constant throughout all of this?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Mental retardation is a constant. However, an alcoholic suffering from alcohol-induced psychosis is a person who -- whose ability to function is, at least in part, permanently affected. There are various segments of functioning, various aspects, and in each one of them, he may present partially-sane, adequate behaviour, but in another part, he would be affected by his condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, could you take now the other exhibit, 877.23? This is your opinion letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we got a little off the schedule with the break. I don't know what the Trial Chamber's preference here is in terms of the next break or I can continue, I can break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How long are you going to be in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm about halfway through my outline, Mr. President. I think if we pressed on, I could finish the cross-examination this evening. If we break for a half hour, I think it's unlikely I would finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to the Prosecutor being allowed so much time, almost twice as much as we had for examination-in-chief. We may take three or four days asking the witness all sorts of questions without ever touching upon the essence of his testimony. That is why I object to such a lengthy cross-examination. I hope you will rule that the Prosecutor will have as much time as we had, no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you ever to understand that this witness is an expert witness and his statement furnished to us, we could read his statement by ourselves. So your job in the direct examination is to draw our attention to the particular points which are mentioned in his report, in his statement. But the Prosecution, the other part, they have to ask a lot of questions concerning this report. But that's different. Well, Mr. Stringer, we could sit until you finish, but that will be too long for the interpreters and for the tape to run. So maybe we could break for 20 minutes and see whether you could finish your cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That sounds fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at 20 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, now I'd like to turn to your own opinion letter. This is the document marked 877.23. I just want to -- and this is actually going to be fairly brief. I want to ask you just a couple of things that are contained in the section of your letter that is the opinion. First of all, right there at number 1, what you said is that with this patient, to quote your words, "The clinical picture is unclear." And it have in the base of it, diagnoses of several psychiatric entities. And then you go on to mention the three conditions that we've been discussing. My question, sir, is: Your statement that the clinical picture was unclear, is that because you had such limited information to go on in even giving this opinion?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: No. I said it because a vague and unclear clinical picture means that it is not clear. It would be clear if we were dealing with only one disorder. That is only delirium or only psychosis or something third. When you have two or three disorders overlapping, then the clinical picture becomes unclear, that is complex.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put it to you this way, then. And actually we'll go to the last sentence of your letter because this is something that you refer to in your testimony and I wanted to make sure we cover that. The last sentence says that a more accurate evaluation of the patient's condition can be produced by the inspection of other medical documentation or psychiatric and psychological examination of the patient himself. So now, recognising, sir, that you did say that, let me ask you this question again: Would the clinical picture have been clearer if you had been given access to more documentation, if you had been given access to the patient himself?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: I believe it would have been as complex but perhaps it would be clearer as to the distinctions drawn among these three disorders, that is which one is the primary one, which one should be accorded greater weight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and then moving down, you've referred to the diagnosis that you were given, the alcoholic psychosis, and again, based on your testimony, I believe it's fair to say that this is a disorder in which psychosis, episodes of psychosis can occur in conjunction with or related to alcohol use or alcohol withdrawal. Alcohol is in one way or the other the triggering event, if you will?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That's right, with one correction. This diagnosis was not mine. This was Dr. Omanovic's diagnosis and I merely quoted it, in a way of speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. You accepted all of his diagnoses without exception, you assumed they were correct diagnoses and then you began your own work?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sticking with the alcohol-induced psychosis, if the witness -- if Mr. Ajanic was not experiencing such an episode in 1993, when the events happened that he testified about, then wouldn't that tend to support the view that he had a greater capacity to form memories of those events?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Well, if not in 1993, if he did not suffer any psychological changes at that time, then yes. If he did suffer any changes, then the answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But we don't really know what was his condition in the summer of 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: We do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what we've just said could also apply to last January of this year, when he came and testified in the Tribunal? If he was not experiencing an episode of psychosis at that time, then that would tend to support the view is that he had a greater capacity to recall memories from 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Regardless of whether in January this year he had or didn't have a psychosis, he was diagnosed with debilitas, with mental retardation which in itself can result in some cognitive dysfunctioning. That is the mental retardation is lifelong thing, if it exists, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, we are going to talk about the mental retardation in a few moments. Let me ask you this about the amnesic syndrome, the amnesia. You mentioned in your direct examination, you referred to the Korsakov Syndrome which understand is a move severe form of amnesia that is related to alcohol abuse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we are clear, the initial diagnoses of Dr. Omanovic, which you accepted as correct, make no reference to Kosakov syndrome?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion in respect of the amnesic syndrome, you said that the causes of such a condition can be in the alcoholic addiction but many others as well. My question, then, is whether in fact in this case, the only condition which is indicated would be the alcoholic condition? There is nothing else that you know about this gentleman that would have suggested an alternative basis for the amnesic syndrome?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: We do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't know it because we only have the information that we got from Dr. Omanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you haven't read the gentleman's testimony. He testified about a number of events that occurred in 1993. The fact that he was able to recall events, the fact that he did not claim that he could not recall, is in fact inconsistent with the amnesic syndrome, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN BEGIC
utterances.text: Well, as you put it, correct, but had I examined this gentleman, perhaps I would have asked him some other things, and then I'd have been able to see whether really --
